basis: Transplacentally acquired autoimmunity; no additional organ is consistently affected across the heterogeneous subtypes.
Progressive cerebral neurodegeneration with dementia; visual abnormalities are occasional and often neurologic.
Intellectual disability, strabismus and skeletal deformities are obligate; obesity alone does not establish endocrine injury.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia affecting cartilage, bone growth and joints.
Glycosylation disorder with encephalopathy; hepatic transaminases elevated in 20/20; anticoagulant deficiencies 30-79%. Damaging ocular findings are occasional.
Inherited sideroblastic anemia; elevated iron indices alone do not establish extrahematologic organ damage.
Brain iron accumulation causes progressive neurodegeneration; retinal dystrophy and pigmentary retinopathy occur in 30-79%.
Defining spinal dysraphism with vertebral closure defect and hypospadias, a urethral malformation; other anomalies are variable.
Congenital herniation of intracranial contents through a skull-base bony defect.
Congenital partial cryptophthalmia affects eyelid formation and the ocular surface.
Basal cell carcinoma arising in penile skin; the cutaneous origin determines the axis.
ATP1A2-related cerebral channel dysfunction causes hemiplegic migraine; nausea and transient visual symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Benign neoplasm originating in the larynx, which belongs to the airway axis.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder defined by infantile encephalomyopathy affecting brain and skeletal muscle.
Recurrent metabolic crises with neurologic regression and mitochondrial myopathy; muscle biopsy abnormalities and weakness support intrinsic muscle disease.
Abstract grouping of syndromes; no particular organ or mechanism applies across the umbrella.
Eye, dental and digital defects define ODDD; neurologic dysfunction occurs in 30-79%. Cap omits hearing loss and hair abnormalities, also reported in 30-79%.
Pontocerebellar malformation with severe neurologic dysfunction; cataract and optic atrophy each 4/8. Muscle atrophy/scoliosis likely secondary to motor impairment.
Reduced circulating red cells, white cells and platelets directly define a hematologic abnormality.
Autoinflammatory interferonopathy; reported rash, organomegaly and hypertriglyceridemia alone do not establish lasting damage to additional organs.
Congenital structural disease of the heart and associated cardiovascular structures.
Abnormal accumulation of histiocytes, cells of hematopoietic origin; tissue distribution varies widely across subtypes.
Inherited neurotransmitter metabolism disorder causing dopamine deficiency, infantile parkinsonism and motor delay.
Intrinsic skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure with loss of ventilatory function occurs in 30-79%. Dysphagia and facial weakness reflect muscle disease.
Isolated congenital ocular malformation with small eyes and displaced pupils.
